requirements: A local, web-based system health monitor. A privileged observer (root, deterministic, read-only) sweeps health, hardware, logs, firewall, networking, processes, services and containers through staggered probes and emits observations to a broker. The dashboard reads and displays them; the judge classifies them through many parallel attestations per context, so relevant events percolate up, reach the dashboard, and notify the desktop when critical. Amortized under 1-2% system load per day.
constraints: The agent runs as root, launched by hand for now, and every action it takes is deterministic and read-only. Only the unprivileged service asks the judge anything. Broker: NATS JetStream on loopback with per-role credentials. Retention configurable, default 7 days or 10 GiB. The judge, when configured, on loopback (default 127.0.0.1:8200), sized for a 16K-token context. Python 3.12, uv.

components.name: schema
components.responsibility: The versioned wire types every process shares: Observation, Finding, Context, Attestation, Issue, Heartbeat, Event; strict encode/decode that refuses unknown fields and kinds.

public_interface.name: Event
public_interface.signature: Event(kind: Kind, at: float, source: str, subject: str, body: Mapping)

components.name: redact
components.responsibility: Removes secret-shaped text (tokens, keys, passwords, env values) from anything leaving the privileged agent.

components.name: config
components.responsibility: Loads and validates the one config file: paths, cadences, CPU budget, broker URL, the judge URL and concurrency, retention (max age and max bytes, whichever first; default 7 days / 10 GiB), notification threshold. Unknown keys refuse.

components.name: probes
components.responsibility: The closed probe catalog: each probe's id, tier, fixed read-only argv, file reads or Docker GET path, cost class, and the parser from raw bytes to observation data. Pure data plus pure parsers; executes nothing.

public_interface.name: ProbeSpec
public_interface.signature: ProbeSpec(id: str, tier: Tier, kind: Kind, argv: tuple[str, ...], path: str, cost: Cost)

components.name: questions
components.responsibility: The question bank: for each context kind (a domain snapshot, or one entity such as a process, unit, container, listener or disk), every typed question worth asking, and what each answer means for severity, cause and next step. Pure data.

public_interface.name: Question
public_interface.signature: Question(id: str, kind: AnswerKind, instructions: str, options: tuple[Option, ...], levels: tuple[str, ...], meaning: Meaning, stability_check: bool)

components.name: bus
components.responsibility: The NATS JetStream adapter, and the only thing that imports a NATS client: stream and durable-consumer setup with retention from config, publish with ack, resumable subscribe.

public_interface.name: connect
public_interface.signature: connect(url: str, creds: Path | None) -> Bus

components.name: store
components.responsibility: The dashboard's query index in SQLite: latest value per probe, rollups for charts, attestations, issues and acknowledgements, and the bounded caches of log explanations by template key and of service descriptions by unit name. One writer (the service), retention from config.

public_interface.name: latest
public_interface.returns: tuple[tuple[float, Observation], ...] (newest first; `at` lets the UI show staleness)

public_interface.name: ack
public_interface.signature: Store.ack(issue_id: str, at: float, by: str = '') -> Issue

public_interface.name: snooze
public_interface.signature: Store.snooze(issue_id: str, until: float, by: str = '') -> Issue

public_interface.name: findings
public_interface.signature: Store.findings(since: float | None, latest: bool) -> tuple[tuple[float, Finding], ...]

public_interface.name: attestations
public_interface.signature: Store.attestations(context, question, since, latest: bool) -> tuple[tuple[float, Attestation], ...]

public_interface.name: incidents
public_interface.returns: tuple[Incident, ...] (link + member issues/findings + missing ids; by severity, score)

public_interface.name: series
public_interface.signature: Store.series(probe: str, field: str, since: float, step_s: int) -> tuple[Point, ...]

public_interface.name: save_log_explanations
public_interface.returns: int (rows removed by the least-recently-seen cap)

public_interface.name: save_service_descriptions
public_interface.returns: rows removed by the MAX_SERVICE_DESCRIPTIONS cap

public_interface.name: service_descriptions
public_interface.returns: cached descriptions by unit name, each with the service key it was written for

public_interface.name: holds
public_interface.returns: each acknowledged or snoozed issue's Hold(by, at, until); by is '' for the dashboard's operator, else agent:<name>

public_interface.name: audit
public_interface.signature: Store.audit(at: float, agent: str, action: str, target: str, detail: Mapping) -> None

public_interface.name: audit_log
public_interface.signature: Store.audit_log(limit: int, agent: str | None, since: float | None) -> tuple[AuditEntry, ...]

components.name: broker
components.responsibility: Runs nats-server for manual mode: writes its config bound to 127.0.0.1, generates one credential per role, and holds the permission policy as data: the agent may only publish observations; the evaluator may read observations and publish judgements and issues; the dashboard and notifier may only read.

public_interface.name: render_config
public_interface.signature: render_config(config: Config, passwords: Mapping[Role, str]) -> str

owns_adapter_to: nats-server process, its config and credential files

components.name: rules
components.responsibility: Deterministic hard alarms over a snapshot: MCE/EDAC, SMART critical, thermal, disk full, crash loops, interface churn, failed units, journald gaps, new 0.0.0.0 listeners, kernel taint.

components.name: judge
components.responsibility: The judge adapter and its own client. Packs each context's questions into as few requests as the context budget allows, runs requests concurrently up to the configured limit, re-asks stability-checked questions with options reversed, and validates every answer against the question asked.

public_interface.name: attest
public_interface.returns: tuple[Attestation, ...] (each carries question, answer, reading, stable, latency_ms)

components.name: notifier
components.responsibility: Desktop notifications for issues at or above the configured severity: one per issue per state change, deduplicated, rate-limited.

public_interface.name: consider
public_interface.returns: Notification | None (None when below threshold, duplicate, or rate-limited)

owns_adapter_to: desktop notifications (org.freedesktop.Notifications on the session bus)

components.name: analyst
components.responsibility: The configured backend LLM, for manual analysis only: an OpenAI-compatible or Anthropic endpoint, local by default. Builds one request from the operator's selection (events, issues, a link, or a time window) plus bounded context, redacts it again, estimates size and destination for the operator to confirm, and returns advisory text. It has no tools and no way to change any state. It also explains kinds of journal line for the Logs view: the uncached templates, packed into as few requests as the budget allows, answered as a JSON object keyed by template key and validated (unknown keys ignored, text bounded). It describes systemd services for the Services view the same way: each service's name, definition and state, keyed by service key, answered as {key: {brief, full}} and validated (unknown keys ignored, both parts required, lengths bounded).

public_interface.name: estimate
public_interface.returns: Estimate (chars, approx tokens, backend, model, remote: bool)

public_interface.name: analyze
public_interface.returns: Analysis (error set instead of raising when the backend fails)

public_interface.name: estimate_logs
public_interface.returns: LogEstimate (chars, approx tokens, backend, model, host, remote, requests, templates)

public_interface.name: explain_logs
public_interface.returns: LogExplained (key -> explanation, model, requests, failed, error; never raises)

public_interface.name: estimate_services
public_interface.returns: ServiceEstimate (chars, approx tokens, backend, model, host, remote, requests, services)

public_interface.name: describe_services
public_interface.returns: ServicesDescribed (key -> ServiceText(brief, full), model, requests, failed, error; never raises)

owns_adapter_to: configured analysis LLM backend (OpenAI-compatible or Anthropic API)

components.name: logs
components.responsibility: The Logs view's reader, in the unprivileged service: runs one fixed journalctl argv on demand (no shell, empty environment, timeout, output cap; the root agent is not involved), decodes each JSON line, redacts every message with redact before anything stores, sends or shows it, and masks a message's variable parts into a template whose short hash keys one kind of line.

public_interface.name: read_journal
public_interface.returns: JournalRead (lines oldest first, skipped, truncated; error set instead of raising)

public_interface.name: parse_line
public_interface.returns: LogLine (at, priority, unit, identifier, redacted message, source, template, key)

public_interface.name: template_of
public_interface.returns: str (numbers, hex, UUIDs, MACs, IPs, durations masked)

owns_adapter_to: the systemd journal, read as the service's user (journalctl -n 200 -o json)

components.name: correlator
components.responsibility: The linking pass. Deterministically proposes bounded candidate groups (shared entity, co-occurrence within a window, known patterns), then asks Judge the correlation bank for every candidate at once, and emits Links. Never changes a member.

public_interface.name: candidates
public_interface.signature: candidates(items: Sequence[Item], window_s: float, limit: int) -> tuple[Candidate, ...]

components.name: executor
components.responsibility: The read-only boundary. Runs catalog entries and nothing else: fixed argv with no shell and no inherited environment; file reads opened O_RDONLY; Docker API GET on allowlisted paths. Timeout, output cap, CPU time measured. Anything off-catalog is refused.

public_interface.name: execute
public_interface.signature: execute(spec: ProbeSpec, timeout_s: float, max_bytes: int) -> RawResult

public_interface.name: RawResult
public_interface.signature: RawResult(stdout: bytes, exit_code: int, cpu_ms: int, truncated: bool)

owns_adapter_to: host probe binaries (ss, systemctl, journalctl, nvidia-smi, smartctl, nft, ip)

components.name: evaluator
components.responsibility: Classification. Keeps a short in-memory window of observations, builds contexts from what changed (one per domain, plus one per entity worth a look), runs rules, asks Judge the whole bank for every context at once, and percolates: deterministic alarms first, then severity by urgency, stability and novelty. A judgement can raise or rank an issue, never clear a deterministic alarm.

components.name: collector
components.responsibility: The privileged observer: root, deterministic, read-only. Staggered, jittered schedule over the catalog; budget accounting that defers probes past the CPU budget; redaction; publishing observations and heartbeats. Runs the write canary at start and publishes whether it is confined.

public_interface.name: Collector
public_interface.signature: Collector(catalog, execute, publish, clock, budget: Budget)

components.name: web
components.responsibility: Loopback HTTP with a per-launch token: read API over the store, a server-sent event stream fed from the bus, and one write, acknowledging or snoozing an issue in the monitor's own store.

public_interface.name: make_app
public_interface.signature: make_app(store: Store, live: Live, token: str, config: Config, analyst, *, judge_health, read_logs, agent_token) -> App

public_interface.name: start
public_interface.signature: start(app: App, host: str, port: int) -> Callable[[], Awaitable[None]]
public_interface.returns: the stop function; binds only the given loopback host

public_interface.name: routes
public_interface.signature: GET /api/overview, /api/issues, /api/issues/{id}, /api/incidents, /api/domains/{d}, /api/series, /api/health, /api/analyses/{id}, /api/logs, /api/logs/explain/{id}, /api/services/describe/{id}, GET /api/stream (SSE), POST /api/issues/{id}/ack|snooze, POST /api/analyses/estimate, POST /api/analyses, POST /api/logs/estimate, POST /api/logs/explain, POST /api/services/estimate, POST /api/services/describe -> JSON

public_interface.name: agent_routes
public_interface.returns: JSON; loopback peers with the agent token and X-Neonwatch-Agent only

owns_adapter_to: local AI agents over HTTP on loopback (the agent API)

components.name: ui
components.responsibility: The functional dashboard: what needs attention now, why (the attestations behind it), the evidence, and the next read-only check to run. Renders only states the evidence supports; stale and unknown are never drawn as healthy.

public_interface.name: contract
public_interface.signature: consumes web.routes; renders Issue, Attestation, Observation, Heartbeat

components.name: service
components.responsibility: The unprivileged composition root, run in your desktop session: wires config, bus, store, evaluator, web, notifier and analyst.

components.name: launcher
components.responsibility: The CLI. `neonwatch broker` and `neonwatch service` refuse to run as root; `sudo neonwatch agent` refuses to run as anything else. Manual launch now; systemd later.

components.name: jobs
components.responsibility: Joins the latest parsed cron and systemd observations into the job and service records the evaluator and the dashboard both read: stable job ids, the static part that is the judge's context state, and the volatile last/next/result. Pure functions over dicts; imports nothing in this design.

public_interface.name: scheduled
public_interface.signature: scheduled(latest: Mapping[str, Mapping[str, Any]]) -> tuple[list[dict[str, Any]], int]

public_interface.name: services
public_interface.signature: services(latest: Mapping[str, Mapping[str, Any]]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]

public_interface.name: service_key
public_interface.returns: 16-hex hash of the service's name, description, exec, file and user

components.name: agent_token
components.responsibility: The local agent API's long-lived credential: one token in a 0600 file beside the store, created by the service when missing (O_EXCL), read with the config loader's care (no symlink, regular, owner, no group/other bits), rotated atomically.

public_interface.name: ensure
public_interface.signature: ensure(where: Path, owner: int) -> tuple[str, bool]

owns_adapter_to: the agent token file in the service's state directory

components.name: mcp
components.responsibility: `neonwatch mcp`: a zero-dependency stdio MCP server (JSON-RPC on stdin/stdout) whose tools each call the dashboard's local agent API on loopback with the agent token and an X-Neonwatch-Agent name; every failure is an isError result.

public_interface.name: main
public_interface.signature: main(config: Config, *, uid: int, agent: str | None, environ: Mapping) -> int
public_interface.returns: int (serves until stdin ends; 2 for an unusable agent name)

public_interface.name: TOOLS
public_interface.returns: status, list_issues, get_issue, acknowledge_issue, snooze_issue, list_services, get_service, list_scheduled, read_logs, estimate_/start_analysis, estimate_/start_service_descriptions, estimate_/start_log_explanations, get_job, audit

owns_adapter_to: the dashboard's agent API over HTTP on loopback (client)

components.name: models
components.responsibility: Which models NeonWatch calls, as the operator sets them from the dashboard: an overlay on [judge] and [analyst] in models.json and the keys in secrets.json, both 0600 beside the config, read with the config loader's care and written staged and renamed. A change is checked whole by the config's own rules (check_analyst, judge_url_problem) before anything is written, then applied live through the service's callback. Keys are never logged or returned.

public_interface.name: Models
public_interface.signature: Models(base: Config, where: Path, owner: int, environ: Mapping[str, str], apply: Callable[[Config, Keys], None])
public_interface.returns: the live setting: load() -> (Config, problems), view(editable, why_not) -> dict, save(change) -> Config (raises ModelsError)

public_interface.name: analyst_key
public_interface.signature: analyst_key(config: Config, keys: Keys, environ: Mapping[str, str]) -> str
public_interface.returns: the dashboard's key, else the api_key_env variable's

owns_adapter_to: models.json and secrets.json beside the config file
